etymology.hint: mouth

characterDeckComponents.note: 口 (mouth) — an interjection like 'oh' is spoken aloud.
我 (wǒ) gives a sound distantly related to ó, having drifted apart over time.
旦 (dàn) gives the sound — 但 is also pronounced dàn, an exact match.

etymology.hint: cloth

characterDeckComponents.note: 衤 (clothing) — 被 originally meant a quilt or covering, like a blanket.
皮 (pí) gives a hint of the sound — 被 is pronounced bèi, a connection that has shifted over time.

makemeahanzi.definition: to walk, to run, to flee

etymology.hint: Someone 土 stepping with their foot 止

characterDeckComponents.note: 土 (here representing a person swinging their arms, not its usual meaning 'earth') — depicts someone in motion.
止 (a foot) — combined with the moving figure above, 走 shows a person walking or running.

etymology.hint: A giant 大 with a normal-sized man 丶 for scale

characterDeckComponents.note: 太 adds a small dot below 大 (big) — the extra mark emphasizes something even bigger or more extreme, giving 太 its meaning 'too' or 'extremely.'

makemeahanzi.definition: unit of distance equal to 0.5km; village; lane

etymology.hint: Unit of measure for farm 田 land 土

characterDeckComponents.note: 田 (farmland) over 土 (earth/soil) — originally referred to a village or a measured unit of farmland, later extended to mean 'inside' or a unit of distance.

makemeahanzi.definition: heel; to accompany, to follow; with

etymology.hint: foot

characterDeckComponents.note: 足 (foot) — 跟 originally referred to the heel of the foot, extended to mean 'to follow (on someone's heels)'
艮 (gèn) gives a loose sound connection to 跟's reading gēn

etymology.hint: Two fish 冉 caught on a line 一

characterDeckComponents.note: 再 depicts something stacked again on top of a base line — repetition, or doing something 'once more,' is pictured by piling on an extra layer.

makemeahanzi.definition: to hear, to listen; to understand; to obey

etymology.hint: Words 口 reaching an ear 斤

characterDeckComponents.note: 口 (mouth) — words spoken by a mouth are what reach the ear, giving 听 its meaning 'to listen.'
斤 stands in for the ear in this simplified character — the target that spoken words reach.

etymology.hint: A decisive 夬 will 忄; 夬 also provides the pronunciation

characterDeckComponents.note: 忄 (heart/mind) — the state of mind being described.
夬 (a decisive, resolute action) — a resolute state of mind, giving 快 its meaning 'fast, quick.'

etymology.hint: speech

characterDeckComponents.note: 讠 (speech) — 谁 is spoken aloud when asking about a person
隹 (zhuī, short-tailed bird) gives a sound distantly related to 谁's reading, though pronunciation has drifted over time

makemeahanzi.definition: much, many, multi-; more than, over

etymology.hint: Two nights 夕, suggesting many

characterDeckComponents.note: 夕 (evening/night), doubled — two nights stacked together suggested the idea of accumulation, giving 多 its meaning of 'many, much.'

makemeahanzi.definition: to use, to employ, to apply; use
below, underneath; inferior; to bring down; next

etymology.hint: One stroke under another; compare 上 (above)

characterDeckComponents.note: A short stroke placed below a longer one — the mirror image of 上 (up), together forming a simple, opposite pair.

etymology.hint: The heavens 一 above a man 大

characterDeckComponents.note: 大 (a person, arms outstretched) — represents a human being.
一 (a line, here representing the sky) — drawn above a person, showing what is above them: the heavens, hence 'sky, day.'

etymology.hint: person

characterDeckComponents.note: 亻 (person) — relates to 像's meaning 'to resemble, be like; image, portrait,' comparing one person or thing to another.
象 (xiàng) gives the sound — 像 is also pronounced xiàng, an exact match.

etymology.hint: One person 人 following another

characterDeckComponents.note: 人 (person), doubled — one person shown following another depicts the idea of accompanying or coming from somewhere.

makemeahanzi.definition: to search for, to look for, to find; change (as in money)

etymology.hint: To go searching with a spear 戈 in hand 扌

characterDeckComponents.note: 扌 (hand) — represents an action performed by hand.
戈 (a spear/dagger-axe) — an old image of searching or probing with a weapon in hand, giving 找 its meaning 'to search, to look for.'

meanings: (before an adjective or verb) to the highest degree

etymology.hint: To take place 取 under the sun 日 (that is, everywhere)

characterDeckComponents.note: 日 (sun) — 最 pictures something happening under the sun, that is, everywhere.
取 (to take, gather) — combined with the sun above, gathering everything under the sun gave 最 its meaning of 'most' or 'the utmost.'

etymology.hint: vigorous

characterDeckComponents.note: 丁 (a stylized handle/hook shape in the ancient form) — part of the character's original picture, now mostly opaque in the modern form
口 (kǒu, mouth) gives a sound related to 可's pronunciation kě, and may connect to 可's sense of approval spoken aloud

makemeahanzi.definition: to do, to act; to handle, to govern; to be

etymology.hint: A man 人 with outstretched arms

characterDeckComponents.note: A drawing of a person standing with arms and legs spread wide — used to represent the idea of something being 'big' or 'great.'

etymology.hint: A person kneeling 匕 before a corpse 歹

characterDeckComponents.note: 匕 (a kneeling person) — a mourner bowed down in grief.
歹 (skeletal remains) — the corpse being mourned, the source of 死's meaning 'to die, dead.'

makemeahanzi.definition: order, sequence; second, next; one after the other

etymology.hint: A person 欠 yawning multiple times 冫

characterDeckComponents.note: 冫 (originally a mark for repetition, unrelated to its later meaning 'ice') — suggests something done more than once.
欠 (a person yawning, mouth open) — repeated yawning gave 次 its meaning of a 'time' or occurrence, as in counting how many times something happens.

makemeahanzi.definition: to go out, to send out; stand; produce

etymology.hint: A sprout 屮 growing out of a container 凵

characterDeckComponents.note: 屮 (a young sprout) growing up and out of 凵 (a container or pit) — a picture of something emerging, hence 'going out.'

makemeahanzi.definition: arid, dry; to oppose; to offend; to invade

etymology.hint: A club or axe

characterDeckComponents.note: A pictograph of an ancient forked weapon, such as a club or shield-tipped spear — the tool image later extended to 干's meanings 'to do, to work' and, in another reading, 'dry.'

etymology.hint: mouth

characterDeckComponents.note: 口 (mouth) — 嘿 is a sound made with the mouth, an interjection.
黑 (hēi) gives the sound — an exact match with 嘿.

makemeahanzi.definition: plural marker for pronouns and some nouns

etymology.hint: people

characterDeckComponents.note: 亻 (person) — 们 attaches to pronouns and nouns referring to people to mark plural, e.g. 我们 ('we'), 你们 ('you all')
门 (mén) gives a sound close to 们's reading (men)

etymology.hint: A spoken 讠 tongue 舌; 舌 also provides the pronunciation

characterDeckComponents.note: 讠 (speech) — 话 relates to speaking and words.
舌 (tongue) — the organ used for speaking, reinforcing 话's meaning of 'speech' or 'words.'

makemeahanzi.definition: and, and then, and yet; but

etymology.hint: A sprout growing in the ground, representing a budding talent

characterDeckComponents.note: 才 depicts a young sprout just breaking through the soil — new growth came to represent budding talent or ability.

meanings: tael, unit of weight equal to 50 grams

etymology.hint: Two people 从 together in a cart

characterDeckComponents.note: 冂 (a covering or frame, here representing a cart) — 两 pictures two things sharing one enclosure.
从 (two people following each other) — together with the frame above, 两 shows a pair joined together, giving its meaning 'two' or 'both.'

etymology.hint: Gold 钅 that once was 昔 but is lost

characterDeckComponents.note: 钅 (metal/gold) — represents something valuable.
昔 (formerly, in the past) — valuable metal that has been mishandled or lost over time gave 错 its meaning 'mistake, wrong.'

etymology.hint: A right hand, representing a pair; compare 左

characterDeckComponents.note: 又 is a simplified picture of a right hand — later used to mean 'again' or 'also,' perhaps from the idea of doing something 'once more' with one's hand.

etymology.hint: Dividing 八 by a line 亅

characterDeckComponents.note: 八 (to divide/split) — represents something being separated into smaller parts.
亅 (a hook/line) — cutting a small piece off, an image tied to the meaning 'small, tiny.'

makemeahanzi.definition: central; center, middle; amidst; to hit (target), to attain; China; Chinese

etymology.hint: A line 丨 through the center of a box 口

characterDeckComponents.note: A vertical line 丨 running through the middle of a box or flag 口 — a simple image for the idea of 'center, middle.'

meanings: by (indicates agent in the passive mood)

makemeahanzi.definition: cry, shout; to call, to greet, to hail

etymology.hint: mouth

characterDeckComponents.note: 口 (mouth) — relates directly to 叫's meaning 'to call out, shout; to be named.'
丩 (jiū) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from jiào.

etymology.hint: mouth

characterDeckComponents.note: 口 (mouth) — 嗯 is a vocalized grunt or interjection.
恩 (ēn) gives a loosely related sound; as an onomatopoeic grunt, 嗯's pronunciation doesn't follow the usual sound-change patterns.

etymology.hint: speech

characterDeckComponents.note: 讠 (speech) — relates to 该's meaning 'ought to, should,' as if reached through spoken agreement.
亥 (hài) gives a sound hint — 该 is pronounced gāi, sharing the same rhyme though the initial consonant and tone differ.

makemeahanzi.definition: rank, grade; same, equal; to wait

etymology.hint: Bamboo strips ⺮ laid before a court 寺

characterDeckComponents.note: ⺮ (bamboo) — 等 pictures bamboo strips, once used as writing tablets, being sorted.
寺 (originally a government office, later 'temple') — sorting and arranging bamboo documents at an official court gave 等 its meanings 'to wait,' 'rank,' and 'etc.'

makemeahanzi.definition: to bring, to grasp, to hold, to take

etymology.hint: hand

characterDeckComponents.note: 手 (hand) — 拿 means to take or hold something in the hand
合 (hé) gives a sound related to 拿's reading ná, from an older, closer pronunciation link

meanings: watch (e.g. of a sentry or guard)

makemeahanzi.definition: more, further; to shift, to alternate; to modify
to help, to assist; to support, to defend; party; gang

etymology.hint: A nation's 邦 flag 巾; 邦 also provides the pronunciation

characterDeckComponents.note: 邦 (a nation/state) — a community bound together
巾 (a flag/cloth) — a banner people rally around to support one another

makemeahanzi.definition: to attack, to beat, to hit, to strike

etymology.hint: hand

characterDeckComponents.note: 扌 (hand) — 打 relates to hitting or performing an action with the hand.
丁 (dīng) gives the sound — 打 is pronounced dǎ, a connection that has shifted in tone.

makemeahanzi.definition: to love, to like, to be fond of; love, affection

etymology.hint: To bring a friend 友 into one's house 冖

characterDeckComponents.note: 冖 (a roof/house) — the home being welcomed into.
友 (a friend) — brought close into one's home; the traditional form 愛 also includes 心 ('heart') in the middle — the source of 爱's meaning 'to love.'

makemeahanzi.definition: belt, strap; band, ribbon; area, zone; to carry, to raise, to wear

etymology.hint: A belt, creasing one's robe above 卅 but not below 巾

characterDeckComponents.note: 巾 (cloth) — the bottom half of a belt, hanging straight down.
Above the cloth, the strokes crease as if folded at the waist — depicting a belt or sash, the source of 带's meaning 'belt, band,' later 'to bring, carry along.'

etymology.hint: A man 干 carrying grain, representing the annual harvest

characterDeckComponents.note: 干 (originally a person) shown carrying a heavy load of grain on their back — since harvests came once a year, the character came to mean 'year.'

makemeahanzi.definition: to ask, to request; to invite; please

etymology.hint: speech

characterDeckComponents.note: 讠 (speech) — relates to 请's meaning 'to request, invite; please,' a spoken request.
青 (qīng) gives a sound hint — 请 is pronounced qǐng, sharing the same base sound with a different tone.
